brief:
Italy's parliament gave final approval to an antisemitism bill that includes a contested definition which critics argue could restrict freedom of expression and Palestinian rights advocacy, Al-Monitor reported. The measure faced opposition from leftist groups concerned about its potential impact on protected speech.

Supporters of the law view it as necessary to counter rising antisemitism, while detractors say the definition of antisemitism it enshrines is overly broad and could criminalize legitimate political speech regarding Israel and Palestinian issues.
dek: By Angelo Amante ROME, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Italy's parliament has given final approval to a bill aimed at combating antisemitism, which includes a contentious definition critics say could limit freedom of expression and advocacy for Palestinian rights.
title: Italy passes antisemitism law despite free-speech objections
